entries.text: Instructions for Recommending New Congregations Table of Contents Requirements for Forming a New Congregation 2 Additional Considerations 3-4 Submitting a Recommendation 5-6 S-50 par. 11. This information should be reviewed by bodies of elders and circuit overseers when considering the formation of a new congregation. When more than one circuit is affected, the circuit overseers involved should work together in preparing the recommendation. RequirementsREQUIREMENTS FOR FORMING A NEW CONGREGATION S-50 par. 22. All the requirements listed below must be met before the circuit overseer submits to the Service Department a recommendation to form a new congregation, whether the new congregation is being formed from a group or from a congregation. S-50 par. 2(1)(1) A significant population—perhaps at least a few thousand individuals—is dependent on the language of the proposed congregation

entries.title: PDF page 1
entries.text: is being formed from a group or from a congregation. S-50 par. 2(1)(1) A significant population—perhaps at least a few thousand individuals—is dependent on the language of the proposed congregation and lives in close proximity to the Kingdom Hall. Thus, it should not be necessary to travel long distances or to spend many hours in search work. If the proposal involves forming a congregation in a foreign or an indigenous language, a significant population in the language community should, in most cases, have little or no understanding of the language of an already established congregation in the area. S-50 par. 2(2)(2) Either there is a significant number of publishers who depend on the language for their spiritual food or Bible students in the territory who depend on and prefer the

entries.title: PDF page 1
entries.text: 2(2)(2) Either there is a significant number of publishers who depend on the language for their spiritual food or Bible students in the territory who depend on and prefer the language are attending meetings and progressing toward baptism. S-50 par. 2(3)(3) A solid core of spiritually mature publishers is fluent in the language. S-50 par. 2(4)(4) There is a sufficient number of appointed men (including at least one elder) to provide shepherding, handle meeting parts, and take the lead in the ministry. (Eph. 4:11, 12; 1 Pet. 5:1-3) In order to provide such spiritual oversight, the majority of the appointed men should be fluent in the language.—1 Cor. 14:9. S-50 par. 2(5)(5) The new congregation is able to conduct all weekly meetings without depending on JW Stream. Local publishers are

entries.title: PDF page 1
entries.text: men should be fluent in the language.—1 Cor. 14:9. S-50 par. 2(5)(5) The new congregation is able to conduct all weekly meetings without depending on JW Stream. Local publishers are able to regularly care for meeting parts. With the circuit overseer’s approval, the congregation may view recorded meetings or portions of meetings on JW Stream on occasion. However, the congregation should not be dependent on this arrangement.—sfl chap. 20 par. 25; chap. 24 pars. 13-14. S-50 par. 2(6)(6) The study edition of The Watchtower and the Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook is available in the language of the congregation or in another language in which the majority of publishers are literate. (If these publications are not available in the language of the congregation, the brothers would participate in the field

entries.title: PDF page 1
entries.text: in another language in which the majority of publishers are literate. (If these publications are not available in the language of the congregation, the brothers would participate in the field ministry, give comments and talks, and pray in the language of the congregation but use publications in the other language during their meetings.) S-50 par. 2(7)(7) A Kingdom Hall or another appropriate meeting place is available for the congregation’s use.

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: ConsiderationsADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS S-50 par. 33. When considering whether to recommend a new congregation, circuit overseers and elders should keep in mind that each publisher or family head must decide which congregation he and his family will attend. No one should be pressured to support a certain language field or congregation.—1 Cor. 11:3; Gal. 6:4, 5; w17.05 p. 10 pars. 10-13. S-50 par. 44. The examples listed below illustrate when a new congregation should not be recommended. Of course, these are merely examples; each situation must be considered individually. S-50 par. 4(1)(1) After one or two years as a group, there are no Bible students attending meetings or progressing toward baptism. Although the majority of the publishers are fluent in the language, only a few or perhaps none depend on it

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: are no Bible students attending meetings or progressing toward baptism. Although the majority of the publishers are fluent in the language, only a few or perhaps none depend on it for their spiritual food. S-50 par. 4(2)(2) A group holds a weekly Life and Ministry Meeting and a monthly public talk in the language. Progressive Bible students are attending meetings. There is a solid core of spiritually mature publishers who are fluent in the language. However, there is only one appointed man, an elder, taking the lead in the group. S-50 par. 4(3)(3) Progressive Bible students are attending a group’s weekly public talk. Although there is a solid core of spiritually mature publishers, most are not fluent in the language and none are dependent on the language. There is an

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: weekly public talk. Although there is a solid core of spiritually mature publishers, most are not fluent in the language and none are dependent on the language. There is an insufficient number of appointed men to provide spiritual oversight. SubmittingSUBMITTING A RECOMMENDATION S-50 par. 55. If it is decided to recommend that a new congregation be formed, the circuit overseer will verify that the information listed below has been prepared accurately before sending it to the Service Department for consideration. Leave the space for the congregation number blank on all forms for the new congregation. S-50 par. 5(1)(1) Congregation Application/Information (S-51) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for each existing congregation involved in the proposal. S-50 par. 5(2)(2) Coordinator of the Body of Elders/Secretary Change of

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: (S-51) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for each existing congregation involved in the proposal. S-50 par. 5(2)(2) Coordinator of the Body of Elders/Secretary Change of Address (S-29) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for any existing congregations in which the coordinator of the body of elders or secretary is changing. S-50 par. 5(3)(3) Kingdom Hall Information (S-5) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for any existing congregations for which the Kingdom Hall information is changing. S-50 par. 5(4)(4) Periodical Request Form (M-202): Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for any existing congregations that are changing their magazine or Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook request. Or each congregation may enter its new or revised requests

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: the new congregation and for any existing congregations that are changing their magazine or Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook request. Or each congregation may enter its new or revised requests on jw.org when the congregation is informed that the new congregation is approved. S-50 par. 5(5)(5) Shipping Information (S-36) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for any existing congregations that are changing their shipping address. Post office boxes should not be used if at all possible. The ship-to congregation in the Kingdom Hall where the new congregation will be meeting should also complete a copy of this form. All updated information, including the shipping address and all congregations in the Kingdom Hall Literature Group, should be listed. This form is required even if literature shipments will

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: this form. All updated information, including the shipping address and all congregations in the Kingdom Hall Literature Group, should be listed. This form is required even if literature shipments will normally be sent to a Regional Literature Depot. S-50 par. 5(6)(6) Territory Adjustment Request (S-6) Form: Provide a completed form for the new congregation and for each existing congregation in which the territory boundaries are affected, carefully following the steps outlined on the form. Since congregation names

entries.title: PDF page 3
entries.text: should reflect their territory assignment, please verify that the names of the congregations involved will still be appropriate once the boundaries are adjusted. S-50 par. 66. The branch office will inform the congregation(s) and circuit overseer(s) if the new congregation is approved. The letter will include the date on which the congregation should begin functioning, along with further instructions. Updated territory assignments and other supplies will follow later. S-50-E 7/21

entries.text: Page 2 instructionsINSTRUCTIONS Fill out a Congregation Application/Information (S-51) form for the new congregation being recommended and for each existing congregation involved in the proposal, as follows: ˙ New congregationFill out the entire form (points 1-8) for the new congregation being recommended. Leave the space for the congregation number blank. ˙ Existing involved congregationFill in only points 1-4 for each existing congregation directly involved in the proposal, namely, those whose territory boundaries are aﬀected or the congregation that has been hosting a group now being recommended as a new congregation. ˙ Name-only changeFill in only point 1 for each existing congregation whose only change will be its name. Congregations requesting a name change not in conjunction with the formation of a new congregation should ﬁll in only point 1. In

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: congregation whose only change will be its name. Congregations requesting a name change not in conjunction with the formation of a new congregation should ﬁll in only point 1. In such a case, the form need only be signed by the Congregation Service Committee. Complete-name rulesCongregation name: A congregation’s name should reﬂect its territory assignment. Each congregation’s complete name is made up of three distinct parts: (1) a directional or other geographic designation (street, park, neighborhood, etc.), (2) a city in the congregation’s territory, and (3) the province or state that city is in. This applies to all congregations, even the ﬁrst congregation in a city. For example, if the ﬁrst congregation in the city of Bath, Maine, has in its territory a principal street called “Hamilton Boulevard,” the congregation

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: the ﬁrst congregation in a city. For example, if the ﬁrst congregation in the city of Bath, Maine, has in its territory a principal street called “Hamilton Boulevard,” the congregation may propose that its complete name be “Hamilton Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Bath, Maine.” (Note: Any directional or geographic names chosen must refer to the city in the congregation’s complete name, not a neighboring city in the congregation’s territory. The name of the city should not be used as the ﬁrst part of the congregation’s complete name.) Existing-name reviewWhen a second congregation is formed in a city where previously there was just one, the original congregation’s name will not automatically be changed. However, the original congregation should request permission to change its name if its current name will no longer

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: was just one, the original congregation’s name will not automatically be changed. However, the original congregation should request permission to change its name if its current name will no longer reﬂect a meaningful portion of its new territory assignment. It may also request permission to change its name if the ﬁrst part of its current complete name is only a language and another congregation of that same language is being formed in that city. For example, if a second English congregation in Smithtown, New York, is formed and the existing congregation named “English Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Smithtown, New York” will now be covering the northern half of the city, it may request permission to change its name to “North Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Smithtown, New York.” Or, if in

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: will now be covering the northern half of the city, it may request permission to change its name to “North Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Smithtown, New York.” Or, if in the original congregation’s territory there is a park called “Mason Park,” the congregation may request permission to change its name to “Mason Park Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Smithtown, New York.” Foreign-language nameIn all cases where the primary language of a congregation is diﬀerent from the principal language of the country, the language must be included in the ﬁrst part of the congregation’s complete name. However, even where there is only one foreign-language congregation in a city, the language should be prefaced by a directional or other geographic designation. For example, if the ﬁrst Spanish congregation in the city of Bath,

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: one foreign-language congregation in a city, the language should be prefaced by a directional or other geographic designation. For example, if the ﬁrst Spanish congregation in the city of Bath, Maine, has in its territory a principal street called “Hamilton Boulevard,” the congregation may propose that its complete name be “Hamilton Spanish Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Bath, Maine.” If in due course a second Spanish congregation is formed in the city, the guidelines in the previous paragraph would apply. Map explanationIf the reason for the name chosen is not clearly identiﬁable on the map provided to the branch oﬃce, please provide a brief explanation of why the name is appropriate. The complete name of a congregation (including the three principal parts described above) should always be used when corresponding with

entries.title: PDF page 2
entries.text: provide a brief explanation of why the name is appropriate. The complete name of a congregation (including the three principal parts described above) should always be used when corresponding with the branch oﬃce, designing letterheads, opening bank accounts, ﬁling exemption applications, and so forth. entries.title: S-51 point 6 — Ashburton 100 km radius research
entries.reference: S-51 point 6 — Ashburton 100 km radius research
entries.text: This aid paraphrases S-50-E (7/21) and S-51-E (1/16). If it differs from current official direction, follow the current official direction.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50
entries.text: Have every involved body of elders and circuit overseer review S-50. If more than one circuit is affected, the circuit overseers work together in preparing the recommendation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Complete one S-51 for the proposed new congregation — points 1 through 8. Leave the new congregation number blank.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Complete one S-51 for each existing congregation directly involved — points 1 through 4. This includes congregations whose territory boundaries are affected and a congregation hosting a group now recommended as a congregation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: For an existing congregation whose only change is its name, complete point 1 only. Check whether revised territory makes an existing name inappropriate.

entries.title: Checklist — S-29
entries.text: Complete an S-29 for the proposed new congregation. Coordinator of the Body of Elders/Secretary Change of Address form.

entries.title: Checklist — S-29
entries.text: Complete an S-29 for each existing congregation whose coordinator or secretary will change.

entries.title: Checklist — S-5
entries.text: Complete an S-5 for the proposed new congregation. Kingdom Hall Information form.

entries.title: Checklist — S-5
entries.text: Complete an S-5 for each existing congregation whose Kingdom Hall information will change.

entries.title: Checklist — M-202
entries.text: Prepare the new congregation’s periodical and Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook request.

entries.title: Checklist — M-202
entries.text: Prepare revised requests for existing congregations whose requests will change. Alternatively, each congregation may enter new or revised requests on jw.org after being informed that the new congregation is approved.

entries.title: Checklist — S-36
entries.text: Complete an S-36 for the proposed new congregation. Avoid a post office box if at all possible.

entries.title: Checklist — S-36
entries.text: Complete an S-36 for each existing congregation whose shipping address will change.

entries.title: Checklist — S-36
entries.text: Have the ship-to congregation at the new congregation’s Kingdom Hall complete an S-36. List all updated information, including the shipping address and every congregation in the Kingdom Hall Literature Group. This is required even if shipments normally go to a Regional Literature Depot.

entries.title: Checklist — S-6
entries.text: Complete an S-6 for the proposed new congregation. Follow every step on the Territory Adjustment Request form carefully.

entries.title: Checklist — S-6
entries.text: Complete an S-6 for every existing congregation whose territory boundaries are affected.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50
entries.text: Confirm that the congregation-number field is blank on every form for the proposed new congregation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(1)
entries.text: Verify a significant population dependent on the proposed congregation’s language lives near the Kingdom Hall. S-50 suggests perhaps at least a few thousand individuals.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(1)
entries.text: Verify the territory can be worked without long-distance travel or many hours of search work.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(1)
entries.text: For a foreign or indigenous language, verify that a significant part of the language community has little or no understanding of the language of an established local congregation. S-50 says this should be true in most cases.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(2)
entries.text: Verify genuine spiritual-language need among publishers or progressing Bible students. Either a significant number of publishers depend on the language for spiritual food, or Bible students who depend on and prefer it are attending meetings and progressing toward baptism.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(3)
entries.text: Verify a solid core of spiritually mature publishers is fluent in the language.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(4)
entries.text: Verify there are enough appointed men, including at least one elder. They must be able to provide shepherding, handle meeting parts, and take the lead in the ministry.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(4)
entries.text: Verify the majority of appointed men are fluent in the congregation’s language.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(5)
entries.text: Verify local publishers can conduct all weekly meetings and regularly care for the parts.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(5)
entries.text: Verify the congregation will not depend on JW Stream. With circuit overseer approval, a recorded meeting or portion may be viewed occasionally, but this cannot be the congregation’s normal support.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(6)
entries.text: Verify the study Watchtower and Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook are available in a usable language. They may be in the congregation’s language or another language in which most publishers are literate.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(6)
entries.text: If publications are not in the congregation’s language, confirm the meeting-language arrangement. Publishers use the congregation’s language for ministry, comments, talks, and prayers, while using the available-language publications during meetings.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(7)
entries.text: Verify a Kingdom Hall or another appropriate meeting place is available.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 3
entries.text: Confirm each publisher or family head is free to choose which congregation the family will attend. No one is to be pressured to support a particular language field or congregation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 3
entries.text: Base projected support on voluntary, individually confirmed decisions — not assumptions or pressure.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 4(1)
entries.text: Check for this warning sign: after one or two years as a group, no Bible students attend meetings or progress toward baptism. Especially significant if most publishers are fluent but few or none depend on the language for spiritual food.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 4(2)
entries.text: Check for this warning sign: activity and progressive students exist, but only one appointed man is taking the lead. The S-50 example has one elder supporting a weekly Life and Ministry Meeting and a monthly public talk; that is still insufficient.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 4(3)
entries.text: Check for this warning sign: students attend, but most mature publishers are not fluent, none depend on the language, and appointed oversight is insufficient.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 4
entries.text: Review the proposal on its own facts, not by mechanically matching or dismissing the examples. S-50 says the examples are illustrative and each situation must be considered individually.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 1
entries.text: Record the proposed complete congregation name. Include the directional/geographic designation, city, and province or state. Leave the congregation number blank.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 2
entries.text: Verify and enter the total active publishers, including pioneers.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 2
entries.text: Verify and enter the figure requested in the form’s “Regular” field.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 2
entries.text: Verify and enter the baptized-publisher figure.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 3
entries.text: Verify and enter the number of regular pioneers.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 3
entries.text: Verify and enter the number of special pioneers.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 4
entries.text: Verify and enter the number of elders who will serve in the congregation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 4
entries.text: Verify and enter the number of ministerial servants who will serve in the congregation.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 2(4) / S-29
entries.text: Identify the brothers proposed to serve as coordinator, secretary, and service overseer in the new congregation. Do this with the host body of elders and circuit overseer. While you remain a group, you do not yet have a separate Congregation Service Committee; the group remains under the host body’s oversight.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 5
entries.text: Write a brief, factual reason for forming the congregation. Continue on page 2 if more space is needed. Tie the explanation to the verified S-50 requirements and the actual local need.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 6
entries.text: List every existing congregation directly involved, with complete name and congregation number. Include each boundary-affected congregation and the congregation hosting the group, if applicable; continue on page 2 if necessary.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 7
entries.text: State when the congregation could begin functioning — the first of a proposed month and year.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 point 8
entries.text: Have the circuit overseer recommend the circuit and section assignment.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Enter the application date.

entries.title: Checklist — S-50 par. 5 / S-51
entries.text: Have the circuit overseer confirm who should sign the proposed congregation’s S-51 before names are entered. S-51 lists the coordinator, secretary, circuit overseer, and service overseer, but it does not explicitly say whether the three congregation signers are the host committee or the brothers proposed for the new congregation. The host congregation also completes its own separate S-51.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Obtain the typed-name signatures confirmed by the circuit overseer. The signature fields shown are coordinator of the body of elders, secretary, circuit overseer, and service overseer.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Build each complete name from three parts: geographic designation, city, and province/state. The first part may be directional or identify a street, park, neighbourhood, or another geographic feature.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51 / S-6
entries.text: Verify the name meaningfully reflects the congregation’s proposed territory assignment.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Verify the first geographic designation refers to the city named in the complete name — not a neighbouring city.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Do not use the city name itself as the first part of the complete name.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: If the primary language differs from the country’s principal language, include the language in the first part.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Place a directional or geographic designation before the language. This applies even if it is the only congregation of that language in the city.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Review the original congregation’s name; do not assume it changes automatically when a second congregation is formed.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51
entries.text: Request permission to rename an existing congregation when its old name no longer reflects meaningful revised territory. Also consider a change when its first name-part is only a language and another congregation of that language is being formed in the city.

entries.title: Checklist — S-51

entries.text: Current control point: The circuit overseer has confirmed receipt of the S-51 and has now requested the remaining S-50 par. 5 forms: S-29, S-5, M-202, S-36 and S-6. He also requested the body’s recommendation(s) for the prospective coordinator and a separate 2026 language-fields information form. A working copy of that return now contains all figures established from the proposal and DeckHand; only the 2026-service-year baptism count is marked TBC. Branch approval under S-50 par. 6 remains pending. Next action: Await Daniel's reply confirming whether the language-fields return should contain only the Ashburton Tagalog Group or cover other fields in the circuit. In parallel, confirm the number baptized in the Ashburton Tagalog field during the 2026 service year, prepare the five requested par. 5 forms, and obtain the body's coordinator recommendation(s). Send nothing further until the completed material has been reviewed and explicitly authorised.

entries.title: Decisions requiring confirmation
entries.text: What date and reporting period apply to the 34 progressive Bible studies? — The number was supplied separately and is not printed in the local proposal or S-303. DeckHand reports 47 total Bible studies for the proposed group in July 2026, confirming that 34 progressive studies is a narrower measure and should not replace the form’s Bible Studies figure.

entries.title: Decisions requiring confirmation
entries.text: Whom will the body recommend for appointment as coordinator of the prospective congregation? — Daniel requested the body’s recommendation(s) as soon as possible in his 25 August 2026 email, citing SFG 1:11, 12.

entries.title: Decisions requiring confirmation
entries.text: Does Daniel want only the Ashburton Tagalog group row or a wider language-field return? — The attached form is generic and plural, but Daniel’s email to Adamson does not state the required reporting scope.

entries.title: Decisions requiring confirmation
entries.text: How many persons were baptized in the Ashburton Tagalog field during the 2026 service year? — The attached form asks for baptisms during the service year, not the total number of baptized publishers. DeckHand’s circuit-assistant export provides a baptism-date column, but it is blank for all 228 Ashburton records, so it cannot establish this figure. The working form correctly marks this cell TBC.

entries.title: Decisions requiring confirmation
entries.text: Approval gate: Both S-51 forms have been sent to the circuit overseer, and S-50 through par. 5 has been confirmed. S-50 par. 6 remains pending until the branch office communicates its decision, official start date, and further instructions.
